title: The Little Cloud Dragon
summary: All the dragons on the mountain breathe fire, except Nubo, who breathes clouds. Until the village below goes weeks without a single drop of rain.

scenes.text:
High up in the mountains lived a family of dragons.

They all breathed fire. With their fire they lit up the mountain at night, like a lamp. With their fire they toasted chestnuts and warmed the stones to sleep on.

All except Nubo, the smallest.

When Nubo opened his mouth, no flames came out. A cloud came out. White, soft and fluffy, like cotton wool.

"Nubo breathes cotton wool!" his cousins laughed.

Nubo tried with all his might. Once, he went red, squeezed his tummy, shut his eyes and blew.

And out came a little cloud shaped like a sheep.

At the foot of the mountain there was a village of colourful houses.

That summer, it hadn't rained even once. The fields were yellow. The river was a trickle. The flowers hung their heads, and the cows looked for shade where there wasn't any.

Every afternoon, a girl called Lucía leaned out of her window, looked at the blue, blue sky, and said softly:

"Please let it rain."

But it didn't rain.

The dragons watched the village from above.

"Poor things," they said. "But all we know how to make is fire. And in this heat, fire is no use to anyone."

Nubo sat on the edge of the rock to think.

He looked at the yellow fields. He looked at the sky without a single cloud.

Without a single cloud.

And all of a sudden his eyes opened very wide.

"I know!" he said. "What they need is clouds!"

His cousins laughed again.

"What are you going to do, Nubo? Take them some cotton wool?"

Nubo didn't answer. He took a deep breath, leaned over the edge of the mountain and spread his wings.

His heart was pounding. But he jumped.

He flew until he was right above the village. From up there, the houses looked like toys.

Nubo took a deep breath and puffed out a cloud. Just one. A small one.

Nothing happened.

He puffed out another. And another. And another. He puffed until his cheeks ached, until he ran out of air, until his head was spinning.

The clouds began to join together. They grew big. They grew grey. They grew heavy.

And suddenly, on the end of Lucía's nose, there landed a drop.

Then another. Then a thousand.

It was raining!

The whole village came out into the street.

The children danced in the puddles. The grandparents turned their faces up to get wet. The flowers lifted their heads, one by one. And Lucía, with her mouth wide open, drank the drops.

It rained all afternoon. And when it finally stopped, over the fields there appeared a rainbow.

Nubo flew back to the mountain, worn out, with aching cheeks and a smile from ear to ear.

His cousins were waiting for him. This time, they didn't laugh.

"Nubo," said the eldest. "Can we come with you tomorrow? After all that water, the village is going to want a fire in every fireplace."

Ever since then, whenever the village sees white clouds coming down from the mountain, they know who's on the way.
